description: Two police officers responded to the same crime — shoplifting diapers. One bought them. The other killed a one-year-old. The choice between those two outcomes is the choice American policing makes every day.

faqs.answer: Kohen Kartier Wiley, a one-year-old boy, was shot and killed by police in Senatobia, Mississippi on June 14, 2026, after officers opened fire on a vehicle in a Walmart parking lot during a response to a shoplifting call over diapers.
faqs.question: What happened to Kohen Wiley?

faqs.answer: Officer Bennet Johns was a rookie officer with the Laurel Police Department in Maryland who, in 2017, bought diapers for a young single mother caught shoplifting them instead of arresting her. The incident received national media attention.
faqs.question: Who was Officer Bennet Johns?

faqs.answer: As of June 16, 2026, no officer has been named, placed on leave, or charged. The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation has taken over the case but has provided minimal information. The Senatobia Police Department has not responded to UnTelevised Media's request for comment.
faqs.question: Has anyone been charged in the shooting of Kohen Wiley?

faqs.answer: The initial police call was for shoplifting — specifically, the theft of diapers (Pampers) from a Walmart in Senatobia, Mississippi.
faqs.question: What was the alleged crime that led to the shooting?

leadParagraph: In 2017, an officer in Maryland bought diapers for a mother caught shoplifting. In 2026, officers in Senatobia, Mississippi shot into a car and killed a one-year-old over the same crime. Both were choices. Only one produced a corpse.

mainImage.alt: Crime scene tape and police vehicles in a Walmart parking lot in Senatobia, Mississippi after a police shooting.
mainImage.caption: Family members of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley speak to reporters after the child was killed by police outside a Walmart in Senatobia, Mississippi on June 14, 2026.

methodology: Reported using original UTM coverage of the Senatobia shooting, WBAL-TV reporting on the 2017 Laurel Police Department incident, AP News, Mississippi Free Press, and WREG News local coverage. UnTelevised Media contacted the Senatobia Police Department for comment and received no response.
title: Two Calls About Diapers: One Officer Bought Them, Another Executed a Baby
